load_bearing_primary.interpretation: A coverage budget is a question about how much of the ASK the model recognised. Charging the tokens of a stated path to it made the verdict depend on the length of the caller's file names rather than on the request. A capability whose own adapter names a module or program that is not there can only fail, so the dependency has to be declared before the refusal can be said early. But the RANKING is a fact about the model and not about the host: this sandbox has pypdf and the CI runner does not, so filtering the ranking by presence made a pinned route hold in one place and fail in the other. The host votes where the work happens -- in solve() -- and nowhere else.
load_bearing_primary.measured_effect: All ten measured sentences naming real absolute paths now route confidently; before, all ten were refused with GOAL_NOT_REPRESENTED_IN_MODEL__FAIL_CLOSED. Coverage on "count the functions defined in the python file <abs path> and write the report to <abs path>" went from 0.240 to 0.714 and is now identical to the same sentence with the paths deleted. Capabilities correctly reporting an unresolvable declared dependency went from 7 to 12 -- PIL x6, chromedriver, crosshair, pandoc, tesseract, pdftoppm, yq/yaml -- every one for a tool genuinely absent. The ranking is host-independent and pinned that way: with every declared dependency on the machine reported missing, 367 of 374 capabilities unrunnable, all four pinned known-goal routes are still confident and still land where the model says. solve() now names the missing dependency instead of spending the request and returning BOUND_PYPI_SOURCE_INCOMPLETE. 15 new tests, 12 of which fail on origin/main; the 3 that pass either way are the negative controls. Verifier 33/33, integrity guard 17/0, artifact byte-identical to a fresh recompile.
load_bearing_primary.stop_condition: STOP when no site raises TEST_PATHS_REQUIRED for a tree that has tests, when a tree with no tests is refused rather than measured as green, when a stated test file still wins over discovery, when the four previously fixed sentences still pass, and when the regression failure SET matches the PR base exactly.

measured_effect: The sentence decides what must change, and the CAPABILITY decides whether it may write the file. 45-request hardcore SWE matrix (fresh tree per case, filesystem / real runner / real command as the only oracles): 8 real answers, 3 false passes, 34 honest refusals, and zero destroyed files. Before this commit the same matrix destroyed 7 files the request had only asked to read or to check (fix <S>, 'the test in <T> is failing...', 'add a test for ...', 'add retry ... to <S>', 'generate tests from the docstrings in <S>', 'the CI is failing because <T> fails', 'count the functions in <S>'), five of the seven reported FAIL_CLOSED over a file that no longer existed and one reported PASS. The rule is not restated in two places: goal_front_compiler_v1.repair_output_collisions now judges the capability's own declaration (capability_edits_source) instead of the sentence's grammar, and composer_route_v1.bind calls it with the entry it is about to run. 'Move the function mul from A to B' no longer licenses deleting A (a move of a SYMBOL is not a move of a FILE): it is now FAIL_CLOSED__NAMED_INPUT_REMOVED instead of a PASS over a deleted module. 'Find every caller of the function add in X' answers from the symbol index and leaves X intact (the word 'add' was read as a change verb; the promise reader now requires the verb to be used imperatively). Suites: test_swe_typed_plan_v1 17/17, test_live_brain_route_admission_v1 OK, test_declared_input_derivation_v1 OK, and the three new suites 12/12, 4/4, 7/7 (4/12, 2/4, 4/7 of their tests fail with the changes reverted). No regression: 373 SWE/front-door test files are 56 red with the changes and 56 red without. Model verifier 33/33 after recompile; drift guard DRIFT_GUARD_PASS on main..HEAD. Zero model dependency, $0. SPEED (2026-10-29): computer_env_v1.discover now refuses before acting when the file it would have to produce is already there; 'Format <S>' went 51,548 ms -> 3,036 ms and 'Replace the magic number 3 in <S>' 33,396 ms -> 1,830 ms at the door, with discover itself 48.7 s -> 5 ms, and the compression goal that really asks for a new file still searches and still closes. New suite test_a_search_never_runs_when_the_target_is_already_there_v1 5/5, and 456 SWE-ish test files are 61 red with the change and 61 red without, zero newly red. A second round in the same PR closed the two ways the door concluded something the world had not said. (1) 'The CI is failing because <test> fails. Fix the build.' returned PASS with python.patch.search.test_guided.ast.v1 whose own payload was PASS__VERIFIED_CANDIDATE_PATCH_FOUND while the named source was byte-identical and the stated suite was still red; stated_application_errors now reads the capability's own provides/keywords -- ...candidate.test_verified does not say applied, ...verified_repair_applied does -- with the one exception of a sentence that states where the REPORT goes. (2) 'Rename the parameter old_price to price in the python module <util.py> and save the report to <out.json>' routed to a Markdown->PDF converter and stopped on Blocker:BOUND_APT_METADATA_NOT_FOUND:pandoc, and the retry that runs python.refactor.rename_parameter.v1 was blocked by executed-is-True; the retry is now refused only where the world was actually judged (observation/truth/promise gates, named judged failure classes, a composed step that RAISED, and any executed failure that did not stop on a stated precondition blocker), so the pinned 'fix <calc.py>' still refuses and the rename is REALLY performed (util.py becomes `def total(price, qty)`, 1,527 ms). An adapter that refuses with raise SystemExit(1) no longer kills the caller: both call sites record it as the failure it is, and the 72-capability classifier test now completes (8/8, an ERROR at the base commit). The 47-request matrix is now execution_guard/swe_capability_matrix_v1.py, which renders the document from its own rows: REAL 9, FALSE 1, REFUSED 37, DAMAGED 0, median 101 ms, p90 912 ms (base of this branch: 8/2/38/0). obs_obs.search_stop_decision: Stop: the sixteen-row census is thirteen of sixteen with zero certified wrong answers and zero destructive rows, and every new postcondition is pinned able to fail.  Measured and deliberately left unserved: the first line of two files at once, a line count over two files, sorting two files together, the lines in both files, the lines in one that are not in the other, and whether one file is larger than another -- each needs a pipeline or an arithmetic comparison, and no single program here does either.

obs_solution.losing_routes_reason: Adding an append-mode writer to the registry loses because it adds a producer to trust where a command and a postcondition suffice.  Refusing the append loses because sed's `r` command performs it and the source survives to prove it.  Widening `find` on the word 'named' alone loses on measurement twice: it answered a deletion of a matched set, and a creation of a folder, with a listing.  Answering a count with `ls` loses because a list of names is not a number and was certified as one.
routes_ranked: sed's r command wins over an append-mode writer, because the source survives and the promise is recomputable
recomputing the promised tail from the source wins over trusting the run, for the reason _post_sort already established
widening the find entry condition wins over adding a second tree rule, because the rule already built -name correctly
scoping the widening away from mutation and creation verbs wins over keying on the word alone, measured both ways
refusing a count of a directory wins over answering it with ls, because a list of names is not a number
comparing the world afterwards wins over comparing the answer, because the defect was a file that no longer existed

obs_verification.synthetic_verification_necessity: Not synthetic: the census runs the real command in a parallel directory and compares BOTH its stdout and the resulting tree file by file, so a row that destroys a file cannot pass however plausible its answer looks -- which is exactly the defect that started this.  The append is asserted on the bytes the destination held as well as the bytes added, and the source is asserted unchanged, so a copy cannot pass as an append.  The postcondition is pinned able to fail from both sides, including a source outside the repository.  The two regressions the widening caused are pinned closed by a deletion that must stay refused with the file still there, and a creation that must still create.
